content.title: Majestic View Nature Center Mural
content.summary: The Majestic View Nature Center Mural, created by artist David Swartz, is a public art project that celebrates Colorado's ecology through a vibrant mural on the storage garage of the Nature Center. The project, initiated by the Arvada Arts and Culture Commission, will be completed by November 2025 and features themes of pollinators, wildlife, and water, highlighting the interconnectedness of local ecosystems.
content.body:
![Nature center with colorful mural of sunflowers, prairie dogs, bees, and hummingbird](/ImageRepository/Document?documentID=6623 "Nature center with colorful mural of sunflowers, prairie dogs, bees, and hummingbird")

The Majestic View Nature Center Mural is a public art project led by the Arvada Arts and Culture Commission in collaboration with the [Majestic View Nature Center](/1215). Artist David Swartz was selected to transform the garage at the Nature Center into an ecological narrative honoring Colorado’s flora, fauna and water systems.

### Location

The mural is located on the storage garage just east of the Nature Center ([7030 Garrison St.](https://maps.app.goo.gl/m77XxgkNKjstkUwf7)).

### Timeline

- August 2025: Artist selected
- Fall 2025: Design and planning
- Fall 2025: Mural installation
- **November 2025: Project completed!**

## About the artist

[Denver-based muralist David Swartz](https://www.daviddoeswork.com/) was chosen through a competitive call for entry judged by the Arts and Culture Commission, MVNC staff, and community representatives for his strong site integration and ecological vision.

Swartz’s work specializes in connecting people with place through narrative-rich murals. His past projects emphasize habitat, species, and layered storytelling tied to local environments.

[![Artist with paint supplies stands beside nature center mural featuring bee and flowers ](/ImageRepository/Document?documentId=6629)](https://www.daviddoeswork.com/)

## Design Concept

Swartz’s design initiative centers on pollinators, wildlife, and water as unifying themes:

- A bumblebee hovers above a fireweed blossom, spotlighting the importance of pollinators.
- Arrowleaf balsamroot flows through the composition, blending into the existing sunflower beds; as seasons shift, a pair of prairie dogs emerge, symbolizing life cycles and renewal.
- A broad-tailed hummingbird moves between fairy trumpet flowers, leading the eye across walls.
- A mule deer amid penstemons and a red-winged blackbird dispersing seeds highlight connections among native species.
- On the final wall, a Western painted turtle ties together the ecological thread, with water streams weaving across all sides to emphasize life’s interdependence.
- The mural will extend onto the ventilation roof and eaves, visually blending the structure into its surroundings.
